text.p: The following are some of the
leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- The army plans to sell tens of thousands of old rifles and pistols abroad as museum pieces, provided buyers do not bring them back into Finand.
- Former President of the European Commission Jack Delors on a two-day visit to Finland will speak in a seminar on the challenges of the economic and social model of the EU.
- Most Finns are in no hurry to know when President will announce plan to run for a second time in office, study shows. - KAUPPALEHTI

- Insurance company Sampo has finally resolved dispute to reduce its ownership. Many shares will now pass to foreign investors, who have increased their share of ownership to over 10 percent in two years.
- Prices of base metals expected to rise next year in line with growth of the world economy, forecasts investment bank Merrill Lynch.
- Many business people are actively seeking seats in municipal councils. Of the total 40,000 candidates in coming elections, up to 3,000 of them are business people. DEMARI
- Finland does not need to rush to link the markka to ERM because of worrying signals from other countries , says second finance minister Arja Alho.
- A flood of illegal medicines is finding its way into Finland through Internet. Orders are placed in electronic mail and the product delivered by post.
